findings.title: Phpinfo Use
findings.description: The phpinfo() function is used to output information about PHP's configuration, which can reveal sensitive information about the environment, such as file paths and database credentials. Removing this function call prevents potential attackers from gathering this information. This fix assumes that the phpinfo() call is not necessary for the application's functionality.
findings.cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
findings.fix_hint: Remove the phpinfo() function call to prevent information disclosure

findings.title: Echoed Request
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks because it directly echoes user input without sanitization. Using htmlentities() function will convert special characters in the callback function to their corresponding HTML entities, preventing any malicious code execution. This ensures that the output is safe to be executed as JavaScript code.
findings.cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
findings.fix_hint: Use htmlentities() to sanitize user input in the callback function
findings.fixed_code: <?php header("Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8"); if (array_key_exists ("callback", $_GET)) { $callback = htmlentities($_GET['callback']); } else { return ""; } $outp = array ("answer" => "15"); echo $callback . "(".json_encode($outp).")"; ?>

attack_chains.title: SQLi to RCE
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses SQL injection to extract database credentials, then uses these credentials to gain remote code execution via a tainted exec finding, achieving persistence on the system. This chain requires minimal skill and results in critical data loss. The attacker starts by exploiting a SQL injection vulnerability in the low.php file.
steps: Step 1: attacker extracts database credentials using SQL injection in vulnerabilities/bac/source/low.php (finding d4adce8d)
Step 2: attacker uses extracted credentials to gain remote code execution via a tainted exec finding in vulnerabilities/exec/source/low.php (finding 7403744b)
attack_chains.remediation: Input validation and sanitization on user input to prevent SQL injection in vulnerabilities/bac/source/low.php

attack_chains.title: Phpinfo to SQLi
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses a phpinfo page to discover database configuration details, then uses this information to perform a SQL injection attack, potentially extracting sensitive data. This chain requires minimal skill and results in critical data loss. The attacker starts by accessing the phpinfo.php file.
steps: Step 1: attacker discovers database configuration details using phpinfo in phpinfo.php (finding d4adce8d)
Step 2: attacker uses discovered database configuration to perform SQL injection in vulnerabilities/sqli/source/low.php (finding 7c5ab1ee)
attack_chains.remediation: Remove or restrict access to the phpinfo.php file to prevent information disclosure

attack_chains.title: Tainted Filename to RCE
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses a tainted filename finding to manipulate file paths, potentially leading to remote code execution via a tainted exec finding. This chain requires moderate skill and results in significant data loss. The attacker starts by exploiting a tainted filename vulnerability in the instructions.php file.
steps: Step 1: attacker manipulates file paths using a tainted filename in instructions.php (finding 02a9e02c)
Step 2: attacker uses manipulated file paths to gain remote code execution via a tainted exec finding in vulnerabilities/exec/source/high.php (finding 5cb3c6b7)
attack_chains.remediation: Implement proper file path validation and sanitization in instructions.php to prevent tainted filename attacks
